qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) Subject:

According to the European Strategy for Housing Construction (COM(2025)0991), around 90 % of construction firms provide services only locally, and only about 1 % of construction services are provided across borders. At the HOUS Committee hearing of 3 November 2026, the Commission stated that the aims of the future Construction Services Act will include the recognition of national certifications related to EU energy legislation and the digitalisation of construction site cards, especially where attendance in person is required to obtain them. For SMEs and workers in Member States with smaller markets, these administrative requirements are often the main obstacle impeding access to other Member States’ markets. 1.
Will the Commission propose that firms and workers from other Member States be able to obtain construction site cards entirely online, before works commence and in a nondiscriminatory manner?

How will the Commission ensure that the facilitation of cross-border service provision does not exacerbate labour shortages in Member States of origin, and what support will it offer in relation to professional training in these states?
